title: Is the prompted detector's inversion (AUROC below 0.5 on machine text) a model-size effect?
lede: does a bigger Qwen make a better human-vs-machine detector? Partly: plain-prompt AUROC rises from 0.278 (0.5B) to 0.329 (1.5B), but 1.5B is still below chance in 84% of family-by-prompt cells.
summary: Replays the first four detector prompts of mimic-anycontext-prompt on its 30 human + 30 RAID machine test texts in each of eight families, with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (Yes/No logit difference, single-text mode). Mean AUROC of the plain prompt is 0.278 at 0.5B and 0.329 at 1.5B; the best of the four prompts reaches 0.296 and 0.389. At 1.5B, 27 of 32 family-by-prompt cells are still below 0.5 (all 32 at 0.5B); only news is near chance (0.504). The sign-flipped score would average 0.72 and 0.67. The 0.5B plain-prompt mean (0.278) matches the earlier project. The gain is uneven: recipes and news improve, books and poetry get worse. Limitations: two sizes of one model family, four prompts, 30+30 texts per family (family AUROC standard error about 0.06), one seed, no selection step. Nothing here is an adapted imitator.
